title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的 Builder 圈在讨论一个深层转变：当模型能力越来越强、成本越来越低，技术本身不再是护城河。Madhu Guru 说这是「有产品感最好的时代」——能做的事情指数级增长，但判断该做什么、怎么组合模型来做的能力，变成了真正的稀缺品。从 Booking CEO 到 VC 到 Box CEO，不同角度的声音汇聚成一个共识：创新速度和对领域的深度理解，比任何技术壁垒都重要。

archive.title: 产品力日报
archive.desc: 技术不再是壁垒，产品感和领域洞察成为 AI 时代真正的稀缺资源：从 Booking 的 27 年起死回生到创业者的「无护城河」觉醒。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-07-22 source feeds.

sections.title: Product Sense is the New Moat / 产品感是新的护城河
sections.desc: Madhu Guru——这位从 Web3 转向 AI 的 builder——提出了一个让所有人停下来的观点：在模型能力拉平的时代，产品判断力是最后一个不被商品化的竞争力。

rewrite: Madhu Guru drops a thesis that cuts against the grain of 'build faster, ship more': it's literally the greatest time ever to have product sense. His logic is counterintuitive but precise—when AI makes execution cheap and abundant, the bottleneck shifts from 'can we build it' to 'should we build it, and for whom.'

A hundred likes on this take suggests it resonated because it names what many builders are feeling but haven't articulated: the tooling has democratized, but taste hasn't. The people who win won't be the ones who can spin up the most agents—they'll be the ones who know exactly where to point them.
original: it's literally the greatest time ever to have product sense

rewrite: Madhu Guru 抛出了一个和主流「造更多、更快」叙事相反的观点：现在是有产品感最好的时代。逻辑是反直觉但精准的——当 AI 让执行变得便宜且充裕，瓶颈就从「能不能造」变成了「该不该造，为谁造」。
100 个赞说明这个观点打中了很多人没说出口的感受：工具已经民主化了，但品味没有。赢的人不是能跑最多 agent 的人，而是知道把 agent 往哪指的人。
original: 毫不夸张地说，现在是有产品感最好的时代。

rewrite: In a second tweet that connects the dots, Madhu Guru argues that the road to AGI is paved with economically valuable tasks—not demos, not benchmarks. That's why enterprise AI is one of the most important frontiers: it's where tasks with real economic stakes live.

This is the practical corollary to his product sense thesis. If you want to build something that matters, go where the money is already flowing and look for the tasks that are expensive, repetitive, and high-stakes. Consumer demos are fun. Enterprise workflows are where value compounds.
original: The road to AGI is paved with economically valuable tasks. That's why enterprise AI is one of the most important frontiers. It's where many of those tasks live.

rewrite: 在第二条推文里，Madhu Guru 进一步把逻辑串了起来：通往 AGI 的路是用有经济价值的任务铺成的——不是 demo，不是 benchmark。这就是为什么企业 AI 是最重要的前沿之一：真正有经济权重的任务都在那里。
这是产品感论点的实操版本。如果你想造真正有价值的东西，去钱已经在流动的地方，找那些贵、重复、出错代价高的任务。消费级 demo 好玩，企业工作流才是价值复利的地方。
original: 通往 AGI 的路是用有经济价值的任务铺成的。这就是为什么企业 AI 是最重要的前沿之一——那些任务就在那里。

sections.title: No Moats, Only Speed / 没有护城河，只有速度
sections.desc: Booking CEO Glenn Fogel 用 27 年从濒死走到 $1800 亿市值的经历，和 VC Nikunj Kothari 对创业者的一句警告，从两个方向击穿了「护城河」这个概念。

cards.authorName: Glenn Fogel, CEO of Booking Holdings

rewrite: Glenn Fogel has one of those career arcs that makes the AI hype cycle feel small. He joined Priceline in 2000—right after the Nasdaq peaked. The stock went from $30 billion market cap to trading at $1 a share. He stayed. A reverse split took it to $6. Twenty-seven years later, it nearly hit $6,000—a thousand-bagger over a quarter century. Last year, Booking did $186 billion in travel bookings, over a billion room nights.

His verdict on competitive advantage is blunt: 'There is no such thing as a moat. There is no such thing as somewhere you're gonna be protected against innovation. Today, we have a competitive advantage on areas. Absolutely. But those can go away tomorrow.' The only durable strategy is continuous reinvention—new services, new ways to do things, every single day.

This isn't defeatism. It's the perspective of someone who's seen a company valued at $30 billion collapse to a few hundred million, then climb to $180 billion. When you've lived through that, you don't believe in moats. You believe in speed, execution, and never getting comfortable.
original: There is no such thing as a moat. There is no such thing as somewhere you're gonna be protected against innovation. Today, we have a competitive advantage on areas. Absolutely. But those can go away tomorrow. The only one to win long term is to continue to develop new services, new ways to do things.

Our stock went from where we were when we went public, we were $30 billion... by the time I joined, we're probably down about $15 billion. In nine months, our market cap is now down to just a couple hundred million. Our stock is now trading at a dollar a share. We do a reverse split. It goes to $6 a share. I stay, and I've been there twenty seven years. We went from that reverse split $6 to last summer, we came very close to $6,000. Up a thousand times.

rewrite: Glenn Fogel 的职业生涯会让任何 AI 炒作周期显得渺小。他在 2000 年加入 Priceline——正好在纳斯达克见顶之后。股价从 $300 亿市值跌到 $1 一股。他没走。反向拆股到 $6。27 年后接近 $6000——四分之一个世纪涨了一千倍。去年 Booking 做了 $1860 亿旅行预订，超过 10 亿间夜。
他对竞争优势的判断一针见血：'不存在护城河这种东西。没有哪里能保护你免受创新冲击。今天我们确实在某些领域有竞争优势，但这些明天就可能消失。'唯一持久的策略是不断重新发明——新服务、新做法，每一天。
这不是失败主义。这是一个亲眼看到 $300 亿的公司塌到几亿、再爬到 $1800 亿的人才会有的视角。经历过这些之后，你不信护城河。你信速度、执行、永不安逸。
original: 不存在护城河这种东西。没有哪里能保护你免受创新冲击。今天我们确实在某些领域有竞争优势，但这些明天就可能消失。长期来看唯一能赢的方法是不断开发新服务、新做法。
我们上市时市值 $300 亿……到我加入时大概掉到 $150 亿。九个月后只剩几亿。股价 $1 一股。我们做了反向拆股到 $6。我留下来了，已经 27 年。从 $6 走到去年夏天接近 $6000，涨了一千倍。

rewrite: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari sees the same pattern playing out in the current AI cycle. His warning to founders: just because there are no moats in AI anymore doesn't mean scale and capital become your new moat. He lines up the graveyard of companies that looked structurally unbeatable—Webvan, Groupon, MySpace, Yahoo, AltaVista, Blockbuster, Nokia, the zombie-corns of 2021—each eventually beaten by a company with a much better unique insight, or simply collapsed under their own weight.

His framework for founders threading this needle: find a unique insight worth a 10+ year journey, while being prudent enough to not let capital and scale become a substitute for it. It's the startup version of Fogel's 'no moat' thesis—applied to companies that haven't even found product-market fit yet.
original: Many founders in the last 18 months are going to realize that just because there are no 'moats' in AI left anymore doesn't mean 'scale and capital' become your main moat. We have seen this movie before. Each one was structurally and capital-wise in a very good position, but eventually got beat by a company with a much better unique insight. Or just collapsed under the weight of their own scale. This is the needle founders have to thread: find a unique insight worth a 10+ year journey, while being prudent enough to not let capital & scale become a substitute for it.

rewrite: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 看到了同样的模式在当前的 AI 周期中重演。他对创业者的警告：AI 没有护城河了，不意味着规模和资本就能成为你的新护城河。他列出了那些看起来结构上无懈可击却最终倒下的公司——Webvan、Groupon、MySpace、Yahoo、AltaVista、Blockbuster、Nokia、2021 年的僵尸独角兽——每一个都是被一个洞察力更强的公司打败，或者干脆被自己的规模压垮。
他给创业者穿过针眼的框架：找到一个值得投入 10 年以上的独特洞察，同时对资本和规模保持清醒——别让它们替代了洞察本身。这是 Fogel「无护城河」论点的创业版本——适用于那些还没找到 PMF 的公司。
original: 过去 18 个月，很多创业者会意识到：AI 没有护城河了，不意味着规模和资本就是你的新护城河。我们看过这部电影。每一个在结构上和资本上都处于极佳位置的公司，最终都被一个洞察力强得多的公司打败了，或者被自己的规模压垮。创业者要穿过这根针：找到一个值得 10 年以上投入的独特洞察，同时对资本和规模保持清醒。

sections.title: The Economics of Intelligence / 智能的经济学
sections.desc: 从 Aaron Levie 的 15X 成本优化到 Garry Tan 的'Compute 决定一切'，今天的讨论在追问同一个问题：AI 部署的成本结构会如何重塑竞争格局？

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie frames multi-model agentic systems as the defining economic pattern of AI deployment. Citing Cursor's new research, he explains the core insight: use a frontier model as a planner and orchestrator, and a cheaper workhorse model for execution, resulting in a 15X improvement in total token costs.

The economic logic is seductive because it mirrors how human organizations already work—senior people make the decisions, junior people execute. But applied to AI, it creates a new kind of business model leverage. Companies that deeply understand their domain AND can route intelligently across model tiers will win workloads that would otherwise be too expensive to deploy. This is the builder version of what Fogel was saying about token economics at Booking scale.
original: Multi-model agentic systems clearly are the future. Great post by cursor. Their new research shows that a frontier model as a planner and orchestrator with a workhorse cheaper model can materially lower the cost of total tokens on a project, resulting in a 15X cost improvement.
This provides the template for where the applied layer in AI will differentiate. You can only drive this efficiency if you know the domain well and have the ability to work with multiple model tiers.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 把多模型 Agent 系统定位为 AI 部署的决定性经济模式。引用 Cursor 的最新研究，他解释了核心洞察：用前沿模型做规划与编排，用便宜的干活模型执行，总 token 成本改善 15 倍。
这个经济逻辑迷人的地方在于，它映射了人类组织已经存在的工作方式——资深的人做决策，初级的人执行。但应用到 AI 上，它创造了一种全新类型的商业模式杠杆。深刻理解自己领域、同时能在多个模型层级之间做智能路由的公司，将拿下那些本来因成本太高而无法部署的大规模工作负载。这就是 Fogel 在 Booking 规模上讨论的 token 经济学的 builder 版本。
original: 多模型 Agent 系统是未来。Cursor 的研究表明，用前沿模型做规划编排、便宜模型做执行，token 成本降 15 倍。这定义了 AI 应用层的差异化——要懂领域、要能在多模型层级之间路由。

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan channels Wu-Tang Clan to make a point that lands harder than any white paper could: 'Compute rules everything around me. CREAM.' The reference is to the 1993 hip-hop classic 'C.R.E.A.M.' (Cash Rules Everything Around Me), and the substitution is deliberate—in the AI economy, compute is the new cash.

With 216 likes, this resonated because it's not just clever wordplay. It's a structural observation: access to compute determines what you can build, how fast you can iterate, and whether your unit economics work at all. In a world where models are increasingly commoditized, the scarce resource isn't intelligence—it's the compute to run it.
original: Compute rules everything around me CREAM

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan 引用 Wu-Tang Clan 的经典，力道比任何白皮书都重：「Compute rules everything around me. CREAM。」原曲是 1993 年的嘻哈经典 C.R.E.A.M.（Cash Rules Everything Around Me），这个替换是刻意的——在 AI 经济里，算力就是新的现金。
216 个赞，这条推文不是抖机灵。它是一个结构性的观察：算力获取渠道决定了你能造什么、迭代速度多快、单位经济模型能不能跑通。在模型越来越商品化的世界里，稀缺资源不是智能——是运行智能的算力。
original: Compute rules everything around me CREAM（算力就是我的 CREAM）

sections.title: Two Kinds of Companies / 两种公司
sections.desc: Coding agent 之后创办的公司从第一天就是不同的物种——这不是预测，是正在发生的事情。

rewrite: Zara Zhang draws a line that's becoming the defining organizational frame of the AI era: there are two kinds of companies now. The ones built before coding agents—scrambling to retrofit. And the ones founded after. The second type is structurally different from day one: teams under ten because they genuinely don't need more, work organized by projects not departments, each person closing their own loop, and almost no internal meetings.

This observation lands because it's not a prediction—it's what Zara is seeing across the builder ecosystem in real time. These aren't just 'leaner' versions of old companies. They're built on a fundamentally different assumption about what one person with agents can accomplish. The old company spent headcount to solve coordination problems. The new company doesn't have coordination problems—each person owns a complete outcome.
original: There are basically two kinds of companies now. The ones built before coding agents showed up, scrambling to retrofit. And the ones founded after. The second type is different from day one: Teams under ten people because they actually don't need more. Work organized by projects, not departments. Each person closes their own loop. Almost no internal meetings.

rewrite: Zara Zhang 画了一条正在成为 AI 时代组织定义的分界线：现在只有两种公司。Coding agent 出现前建的——忙着补课改造。以及之后建的。后者的结构从第一天就不一样：团队不到十人，因为真不需要更多；工作按项目组织，不是按部门；每个人闭环完成自己的工作；几乎没有内部会议。
这个观察能打动人因为不是预测——是 Zara 在 builder 生态里实时看到的。这些不是旧公司「更精干」的版本。它们建立在一个完全不同的人机协作假设上。旧公司用增加人头来解决协调问题。新公司没有协调问题——每个人拥有一个完整的产出。
original: 现在只有两种公司：coding agent 出现前建的（忙着补课改造），和之后建的。后者从第一天就不同：团队不到十人（不需要更多），按项目不按部门，每人闭环，几乎没有内部会议。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch's viral post with 4300 likes makes the connection explicit: 'The big lesson from AI is that everything is code. A slide deck is code. Design is code. That cool promo video? Code. Excel automation? Code. The universe? Probably made of code too.'

This is the technical corollary to Zara's organizational thesis. If everything is code, then one person with agents can produce across every medium—text, design, video, automation. The company that needs five specialists becomes the company that needs one person with taste and a good prompt. The implication isn't just about headcount reduction. It's about a fundamental shift in what 'building' means.
original: The big lesson from AI is that everything is code. A slide deck is code. Design is code. That cool promo video? Code. Excel automation? Code. The universe? Probably made of code too.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 这条 4300 赞的爆款推文把连接点明了：「AI 最大的教训就是，万物皆代码。slide deck 是代码。设计是代码。那个酷炫的视频？代码。Excel 自动化？代码。宇宙？大概也是代码。」
这是 Zara 组织论的技术版本。如果万物都是代码，那么一个人加 agent 就能横跨所有媒介产出——文字、设计、视频、自动化。需要五个专才的公司变成了需要一个有品味、会写 prompt 的人的公司。这不只是减员的问题。这是对「做东西」这件事根本定义的改变。
original: AI 最大的教训：万物皆代码。slide deck 是代码。设计是代码。酷炫视频？代码。Excel 自动化？代码。宇宙？大概也是代码。

sections.title: The China Question / 中国模型冲击
sections.desc: 硅谷对中国开源模型的态度变了——从否认变成了紧张的承认。这场竞争不再只是 benchmark 的较量。

rewrite: Peter Yang drops the most quotable geopolitical AI take of the cycle with 1019 likes: 'Banning Chinese models will be the same self own as banning Chinese EVs.' The comparison is precise: blocking affordable Chinese cars left Western consumers with fewer choices and slower adoption. Blocking Chinese AI models would do the same for builders—depriving them of some of the most capable and cost-effective tools in the stack.

This isn't abstract policy talk. For anyone building cost-sensitive AI applications today, access to Chinese open-source models is a real part of the toolkit calculus. A ban wouldn't just be symbolic—it would be a structural cost disadvantage.
original: Banning Chinese models will be the same self own as banning Chinese EVs.

rewrite: Peter Yang 给出了这个周期里最值得引用的地缘 AI 判断，1019 赞：「封禁中国模型，会和封禁中国电动车一样，是自己坑自己。」类比是精准的：阻挡便宜的中国电动车让西方消费者选择更少、普及更慢。封禁中国 AI 模型对 builder 的影响是一样的——剥夺他们拿到整个工具链里最有能力和最具性价比选项的权利。
这不是抽象的政策讨论。对任何今天在做成本敏感型 AI 应用的人来说，能否使用中国开源模型，是真实工具链计算的一部分。禁令不只是象征性的——它会变成一个结构性的成本劣势。
original: 封禁中国模型，会和封禁中国电动车一样是自己坑自己。

rewrite: FirstMark partner Matt Turck—author of the definitive AI MAD landscape—captures the shift in sentiment with a meme: 'OpenAI and Anthropic when a top free Chinese open source model drops. 😱' The dread emoji is the story. This isn't about benchmark scores anymore. Each new Chinese open-source release narrows a gap that billions of dollars were supposed to widen.

What's new is that even the strongest institutional voices of Western AI leadership are publicly acknowledging the pressure. The conversation has moved from 'can they compete' to 'what happens when the gap closes.'
original: OpenAI and Anthropic when a top free Chinese open source model drops 😱

rewrite: FirstMark 合伙人 Matt Turck——AI MAD 全景图的作者——用一个 meme 捕捉了情绪的转变：「又一个顶尖免费中国开源模型发布时，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的反应。😱」惊恐 emoji 就是全部故事。这已经不只是 benchmark 数字的问题。每一个新的中国开源发布，都在缩小那些本应被数百亿美元投资拉开的差距。
新意在于：连最坚定拥护西方 AI 领导地位的人都在公开承认压力。讨论已经不只是「他们能不能竞争」，而是「差距追上之后会发生什么」。
original: OpenAI 和 Anthropic 看到又一个顶尖免费中国开源模型发布时的反应 😱
